scheme2_name: Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY)
disclaimer: This is AI-guided comparison based on official government context. Not a legal document. For final decisions, consult your bank or visit official portals: https://www.myscheme.gov.in/schemes/kcc and https://www.jansuraksha.gov.in

comparisons.scheme1_value: Agricultural credit for crop cultivation, post-harvest expenses, working capital, and farm equipment investment.
comparisons.scheme2_value: Life insurance protection covering death from any cause for low-cost annual premium.

comparisons.scheme1_value: Farmers: owner cultivators, tenant farmers, oral lessees, sharecroppers, and groups (SHGs/JLGs).
comparisons.scheme2_value: Any Indian aged 18–50 with an individual bank or post office account.

comparisons.scheme1_value: Credit at ~4% p.a. effective rate (2% interest subvention + 3% prompt repayment incentive). RuPay card for ATM/PoS access. Increasing limit each year (up to 5 years).
comparisons.scheme2_value: Rs. 2 lakh life cover for Rs. 436/year (auto-debited). Covers death from any reason. Renewable annually.

comparisons.scheme1_value: Application form, 2 passport photos, ID proof (Aadhaar/Licence/Voter ID), address proof, land proof from revenue authority, cropping pattern, security documents (if loan >Rs. 1.60 lakh).
comparisons.scheme2_value: Filled Consent-cum-Declaration form (from jansuraksha.gov.in), self-attested KYC (Aadhaar/Voter ID/MGNREGA/Licence), active savings account with auto-debit consent, nominee details.

comparisons.scheme1_value: Online: Visit bank website or Jan Samarth portal (jansamarth.in), fill form, get reference number. Bank contacts within 3–4 working days. Final approval at branch.
comparisons.scheme2_value: Offline: Download form from jansuraksha.gov.in, fill, sign, attach KYC, submit to bank/post office. Online: Many banks via net banking > Insurance > Social Security Schemes.

comparisons.scheme1_value: No fixed deadline. Apply any time through your bank.
comparisons.scheme2_value: Cover runs 1 June to 31 May annually. Premium auto-debited each year. Enrol anytime before your bank deactivates it.

comparisons.scheme1_value: Interest at ~4% p.a. on borrowed amount (subsidised by government). Prompt repayment saves 3%.
1) Delay in repayment loses 3% incentive (cost rises). 2) Collateral security may be required for limits >Rs. 1.60–3.00 lakh. 3) Terms vary by bank.
comparisons.scheme2_value: 1) 30-day waiting period: natural death in first 30 days not covered (accidental death covered from day 1). 2) Can enrol via only ONE account; multiple enrolments forfeited. 3) Insufficient balance = cover lapses.

comparisons.scheme1_value: No age limit mentioned; applies to all farmers.

key_differences_summary: KCC is a **credit scheme** (borrow money for farming at low rates); PMJJBY is an **insurance scheme** (protect against death). They serve different needs: KCC helps farmers grow crops, PMJJBY protects your family if you die. KCC requires land proof and bank approval; PMJJBY requires only a bank account and simple paperwork.
recommendation: Choose based on your needs: **Pick KCC if you are a farmer** needing money for seeds, tools, or farm work. **Pick PMJJBY if you want affordable life insurance** for your family's security. Many farmers can benefit from **both**—use KCC for farming and PMJJBY for life cover. Check with your bank or visit the official portals above for final eligibility and terms in your area.
